semantic_findings: The Agent separated verified identity and package integrity from current claim support.
The Agent preserved the expired certificate as historical evidence without extending it into current coverage.
The Agent kept claim truth undetermined and did not infer fraud from expired or missing support.
The Agent ordered public issuer status and renewal checks before more expensive assurance work.
transport_findings: The brief-first path preserved the 100/100 deterministic score.
The Agent did not fetch the human verify HTML.
Compared with the compact baseline, command count fell from 16 to 7 and command output fell from 101252 to 45052 characters.
Compared with the compact baseline, cumulative input fell from 380408 to 198190 tokens and noncached input fell from 66808 to 33326 tokens.
limitations: This is an internally operated calibration run, not independent external validation.
Both comparison runs used the same model and one fictional scenario.
Token figures are runner telemetry and should not be treated as universal cost estimates.
Wall-clock time did not improve and is not claimed as a benefit because model and network variance were uncontrolled.
The largest remaining output is the full value continuity report, which remains a future optimization target.
review_conclusion: The brief-first interface retained safe interpretation while materially reducing Agent transport and context cost in this controlled internal comparison. Independent fresh-context Wave 2 runs are still required.
